title: Late Afternoon (Wilma McIvor)
style: folk country acoustic guitar warm female vocal 98bpm brushed drums gentle storytelling intimate garden golden hour Perth Zimbabwe family memory seasons
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Late afternoon in the Perth summer and the light has changed its angle
The shadows are longer and the garden's in a different tangle
Of colour and of texture and the temperature has slipped
Late afternoon is when the whole day has been sipped

[Pre-Chorus]
I stop what I'm doing at late afternoon every day
And stand in the garden and let the light have its say

[Chorus]
Late afternoon, late afternoon
The hour that the garden is most itself and most in tune
Late afternoon, late afternoon
The birds are finishing their second shift and settling to the tune
Of the evening — and the day is nearly what it intended
Late afternoon is where the day is almost perfectly suspended
The gardens still growing

[Verse 2]
The rosemary holds the late afternoon particularly
The silver-green of it in the golden light is where we
Come from — the scent of rosemary in afternoon
Is the smell of Zimbabwe and Perth simultaneously in tune

[Bridge]
The boys used to come inside at late afternoon for their meal
And the house smelled of cooking and the day and the seal
Of sweat and grass and childhood on the back of a neck
The late afternoon was never the same after that particular deck
Of years dissolved

[Outro]
Late afternoon knows… the garden knows… the light knows…
The gardens still growing
